clue.text: Suspected slight fog caused deterioration

parts.note: a mist is a thin, light fog
rusted means corroded, metal wearing away over time

explanation.surface: Someone blames a light fog for some damage that set in.
explanation.definitionFit: To be suspected is to be doubted or not believed, which is what distrust means.

clue.text: Pound meal-starter remains

indicators.note: the starter of the meal is its opening letter

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A heap of crushed leftovers before dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound food is to crush it to a pulp.

clue.text: Sell now at newly-built block

indicators.note: newly built means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An estate agent selling a brand-new apartment block.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to obstruct or stall, as in blocking questions.

clue.text: Such a comment will get a guy up!

definitions.text: Such a comment will get a guy up!

parts.words: Such a comment will get a guy up!
parts.note: read as a remark added to a document, and also as a person who climbs into a saddle

explanation.surface: A remark that annoys a man.
explanation.definitionFit: An added clause or comment is one sense; someone mounting a horse is the other.

clue.text: Walks over to make connection

explanation.surface: Someone tramples on a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words it means treads on; as one word it is a family relation by marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Treads on is a synonym of walks over; a spouse's son is a relative, a connection by marriage.

clue.text: Finish up without a suit packed

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: to end is to finish up
a case is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Finishing a trip with clothes packed but no suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enclosed in a box or cover is boxed up, wrapped.

clue.text: Some cooking equipment over tips

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the following word end to end, read in the other direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of kitchen kit keeps tipping over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie skewer for roasting meat over a fire is one item of kitchen gear.

clue.text: Aim for the head

explanation.surface: Target the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Aim means purpose, as in 'what's the aim'; a head is a headland jutting into the sea.

clue.text: A painter may have to rent it to work

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist might have to let out a property to earn a living.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance artist of that name is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Does nothing through a setback

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
per means by way of or through
read as set back, the word set turned round

explanation.surface: Does nothing in the face of a reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' is read as two words: set, reversed, giving TES.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate a machine is to work it, so does here means performs or works.

clue.text: Reprimand a little fellow if he's coldish

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of the following words is taken, the run sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Telling off a small boy because he feels a bit chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks you to picture a shivering boy; the answer instead sits inside 'he's coldish', with 'fellow if' as connecting words.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand is to tell someone off, to rebuke them.

clue.text: Being debarred, raises objection

explanation.surface: Someone barred from entry kicks up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense comes from the idiom 'take exception', meaning to object.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion from a rule is one sense; in 'take exception' the word stands for an objection or complaint.

clue.text: Repeats about forces

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
to prise is to lever or force something open

explanation.surface: Military forces rehearsed over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer or actor reprises a song or role when performing it again.

clue.text: The relationship established at entering a foreign port

indicators.note: entering means one word goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
taken as written

explanation.surface: Diplomatic ties are set up when a ship enters an overseas harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion, such as three to one, expresses how two quantities relate.

clue.text: Taking a rug, eat outside perfect!

indicators.note: outside means the word for eat surrounds the other

parts.note: to consume is to eat
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: Picnickers spread a rug and eat outdoors: perfect!
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate skill is complete, flawless skill.

clue.text: Speaking or getting into a mess

annotationWithheld.why: Speaking or getting into a mess: ORATION is O + RATION, but 'or' gives two letters, and no reading puts OR into a word for mess to give ORATION; the clue looks misread or misprinted
annotationWithheld.clue: Speaking or getting into a mess

clue.text: Some leftists would limit a Tory follower

indicators.note: some marks part of the run of words as the answer, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Left-wingers would like to restrain a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A copier follows the example set by someone else.

clue.text: American lawyer of the list may be given time!

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US public prosecutor
a table is a list of figures or names set out in order

explanation.surface: A US attorney on the roster may be offered extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can have a date assigned to it, such as an old artefact, can be given its period.

clue.text: The warder who's not a vegetarian

explanation.surface: A prison guard who eats meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders who guard the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London have this nickname; literally it is a carnivore.

clue.text: Throw in a Spanish article looking for a buyer

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to sling is to hurl or throw
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Tossing in a Spanish item to tempt a customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Offering goods on the market means trying to find someone to purchase them.

clue.text: Tearing around to find the hard stuff

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Rushing about looking for strong drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The hard stuff' suggests spirits; it is a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock is famously tough and durable.

clue.text: Check on a six-footer grabbing small page

indicators.note: grabbing means the creature takes hold of a letter, enclosing it

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so is jokingly a six-footer
p is the usual abbreviation for page

explanation.surface: Keeping an eye on a tall person who snatches a young servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; it is a creature with six feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely is to check it over.

clue.text: One thousand newsmen united to strike

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
the press is the collective term for journalists

explanation.surface: Reporters band together to walk out.
explanation.definitionFit: To stamp a mark onto a surface is to strike it into the material.

clue.text: She gives many a solo

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so stands for many
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A singer who performs plenty of solos.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name stands in for any woman, as 'she' does.

clue.text: Regret accepting some decoration or other

indicators.note: accepting means the word for regret takes the other inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret
CH is Companion of Honour, a British decoration

explanation.surface: Sorry to receive an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or other' means a decoration of another kind, a gathered frill.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered strip of fabric trims a garment, another kind of ornament.

clue.text: When parking in front of house, persuaded to reverse -such a bloomer!

indicators.note: in front of places the earlier pieces before the next one

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: to reverse tells us the word for persuaded is read backwards

parts.note: led means guided or persuaded

explanation.surface: A driver, coaxed into reversing when parking outside a house, makes a howler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reverse' turns LED into DEL. 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphodel is a lily-like plant, so it is something that flowers.

clue.text: Best for a picnic?

explanation.surface: The finest thing for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to beat them; an out-do is jokingly an outdoor party.

clue.text: The odd English set-up in the Netherlands

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: mad means strange or odd

explanation.surface: A strange English arrangement found in Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns MADE to give the Dutch town.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheese town of that name is a place found in Holland.

clue.text: A recluse taking tea, no rich spread

indicators.note: spread means the letters are scattered and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A hermit has tea but nothing lavish to go with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit who withdraws from society for religious reasons is a solitary person.

clue.text: The child a leading journalist bore

parts.note: a tot is a small child
ED is short for editor, the senior journalist

explanation.surface: A youngster that a newspaper chief carried.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore here is the past tense of bear, meaning carried, as does lugged.

clue.text: Quarters for sheep

parts.note: the compass quarters east, west, east again and south, each abbreviated to its initial
the compass quarters east, west, east again and south, each abbreviated to its initial
the compass quarters east, west, east again and south, each abbreviated to its initial
the compass quarters east, west, east again and south, each abbreviated to its initial

explanation.surface: Lodgings for a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: Female sheep are the plural noun here.

clue.text: A record that gives one the shudders!

definitions.text: A record that gives one the shudders!

parts.words: A record that gives one the shudders!
parts.note: read not as a scary disc but as a chart traced by an instrument when the ground trembles

explanation.surface: A frightening record.
explanation.definitionFit: The trace made by an instrument logging earthquakes records tremors of the earth.
